backdrop.rule: The 12 doors of the hill's rows (backdrop_rise_approach_e0 e1, w0 to w4, x0 to x4) are seen at 44 m and more: leaf kind and paint, nothing else. Door i takes kind BACKDROP_KINDS[i mod 6] and paint BACKDROP_PAINTS[(i + 2) mod 6], so that no two doors of a row, taken in their order, share a kind or a paint. No furniture, no step, no wear mask beyond the foot band.

mix_rule.text: A new house takes a kind its frame set allows (cottage frame T: T1 T2 T3; flat frame F: F1 to F7), a paint that is not its neighbours' on the same side nor the paint of a door within 4.6 m across the street, and furniture so that each neighbour differs in at least 2 of the slots letter plate, handle, latch, number. A modernised house (replacement windows) takes T3, F5 or F6 or keeps its old kind. Knockers, bells (except T1's oblong), black iron plates, bell pulls, frosted and wired glass and numerals in black metal are not placed on any house today.

could_not_settle: No dated photograph read shows a door knocker, a bell pull, a black iron letter plate, frosted or wired door glass, or a ledged service door on these streets. KN1, KN2, BL2, LP3, frosted, wired and NM2 are listed with Judgement sizes and refused on every house by the checks; F7 is built from Hasluck and Judgement alone.

Door colours of 1990: the slides of 1975 to 1994 shift hue and exposure, so the palette's bright and mid values (turquoise, bright blue, lime, khaki, mustard, olive) are Judgement from boxes whose medians are recorded; the dark classics are 3.1's.
Small hardware at 22 to 27 mm a pixel (plates, levers, a small light) carries +-24 to +-35 mm; the positions are fractions of the visible face with that error written in each check.
D1's doors stand in deep recesses and are seen from the right: only their vertical rows are used; the leaves' widths and the letter plate's length are not taken from it.
Whether the west shop row (one storey in the drawn street) has flats: its side doors are 1 service door and 2 household doors until Jafar answers owed line 3.
The painted cement hoods over Hull doorways (D1, D6) and their arched recesses (D7) are wall features; not in the door piece, listed for the wall kit.
A house number's digits are the town's; the target fixes only the form (NM1, NM3, NM4).
The shopfront kit's own side door at east_parade bay 2 (Rita's) has its own geometry and a fanlight (unit 2.2); this target gives it kind F1 and expects the builder to put F1's leaf in that slot.
